en.greeting: Hi! Today we learn the small words that say when and where: at, on, in, under, next to and more. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: at, on, in for time
steps.text: When does it happen? English uses three small words for time.
steps.body: **at** + an exact time: **at seven o'clock**, **at noon**. **on** + a day or a date: **on Monday**, **on 1 May**. **in** + a longer time (a month, a year or a season): **in May**, **in 2026**, **in the dry season**. Think small to big: **at** a point on the clock → **on** one day → **in** a long time. Indonesian often says just *hari Senin* or *bulan Mei* (or *pada*), but English needs the small word.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: A national day in April. Which word fits?

question.explanation: **21 April** is a date, and dates take **on**. **in** is for the whole month (*in April*), and **at** is for a clock time.

steps.title: Morning, night and the weekend
steps.text: Now some everyday time phrases. Learn them as chunks.
steps.body: Parts of the day take **in the**: **in the morning**, **in the afternoon**, **in the evening**. A morning is shorter than a day, so this breaks 'small to big': just learn these as fixed chunks. Night is different: **at night** (like *at noon*, *at midnight*). Saturday and Sunday: **at the weekend** (British) or **on the weekend** (American). When you name the day, the day decides: **on Friday evening**. No preposition before **this, every, tomorrow**: *this morning*, *every Sunday*.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Budi is busy all week. When does he play futsal?

question.prompt: Complete: Budi plays futsal with his friends ___ the weekend.
question.explanation: Say **at the weekend** (British English). American English says **on the weekend**, which is also correct. 'in the weekend' is a common mistake, and **to** doesn't go with time here. Both British and American English are fine; just choose one and use it.

steps.title: Where is it?
steps.text: Now let's talk about places. Where is your phone right now?
steps.body: Use **be** (is / are) + a place word: **in** (inside), **on** (on a surface, touching it: *on the table*, *on the wall*), **under**, **next to**, **between** (two things: *between A and B*) and **behind**. These small words are called **prepositions** (*preposisi*). Indonesian says *di bawah*, *di sebelah*, but in English the preposition already includes the *di*: **under the table**, not 'in under the table'.

steps.title: Around the house
steps.text: Here are the place words in a real home. Some use there is / there are from the last lesson.
steps.body: **between** always needs two things: *between the window and the door*. And **on** isn't only *di atas*: a clock **on** the wall touches the wall.

examples.en: The milk is in the fridge.
There is a clock on the wall.
There are two cats under the car.
examples.id: Ada dua kucing di bawah mobil.

examples.en: My desk is between the window and the door.
examples.id: Mejaku di antara jendela dan pintu.

examples.en: The garden is behind the house.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: You can't find your phone. Your mum knows where it is.

options: Your phone is under the pillow.
Your phone is in under the pillow.
Your phone is on the pillow.
question.prompt: Which sentence means 'HP-mu di bawah bantal'?
question.explanation: **di bawah** = **under**. English has no separate word for *di*: **under** already means *di bawah*. So use one preposition only: **under the pillow**. 'in under' adds an extra word, and **on** means di atas.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Rina shows you her new house.

question.solution: The bathroom is next to my bedroom.
question.prompt: Arrange the words: Kamar mandinya di sebelah kamar tidurku.
question.explanation: **di sebelah** = **next to** (two words). The pattern is thing + **is** + place word: **The bathroom is next to my bedroom.**

steps.text: Flip through these cards to remember the small words.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita belajar kata-kata kecil untuk mengatakan kapan dan di mana: at, on, in, under, next to dan lainnya. Ayo kita pelajari pelan-pelan.

steps.title: at, on, in untuk waktu
steps.text: Kapan terjadinya? Bahasa Inggris memakai tiga kata kecil untuk waktu.
steps.body: **at** + waktu yang tepat: **at seven o'clock**, **at noon**. **on** + hari atau tanggal: **on Monday**, **on 1 May**. **in** + waktu yang lebih panjang (bulan, tahun atau musim): **in May**, **in 2026**, **in the dry season**. Pikirkan dari kecil ke besar: **at** satu titik di jam → **on** satu hari → **in** waktu yang panjang. Bahasa Indonesia sering cukup bilang *hari Senin* atau *bulan Mei* (atau pakai *pada*), tapi bahasa Inggris butuh kata kecil itu.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Hari nasional di bulan April. Kata mana yang cocok?

question.explanation: **21 April** adalah tanggal, dan tanggal memakai **on**. **in** untuk satu bulan penuh (*in April*), dan **at** untuk jam.

steps.title: Pagi, malam dan akhir pekan
steps.text: Sekarang beberapa ungkapan waktu sehari-hari. Hafalkan sebagai satu kesatuan.
steps.body: Bagian hari memakai **in the**: **in the morning**, **in the afternoon**, **in the evening**. Pagi lebih pendek dari satu hari, jadi ini tidak ikut aturan 'kecil ke besar': hafalkan saja sebagai ungkapan tetap. Malam berbeda: **at night** (seperti *at noon*, *at midnight*). Sabtu dan Minggu: **at the weekend** (Inggris Britania) atau **on the weekend** (Inggris Amerika). Kalau kamu menyebut nama harinya, harinya yang menentukan: **on Friday evening**. Tanpa preposisi (kata kecil seperti at/on/in) sebelum **this, every, tomorrow**: *this morning*, *every Sunday*.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Budi sibuk sepanjang minggu. Kapan dia main futsal?

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Budi plays futsal with his friends ___ the weekend.
question.explanation: Ucapkan **at the weekend** (Inggris Britania). Inggris Amerika memakai **on the weekend**, dan itu juga benar. 'in the weekend' adalah kesalahan yang sering terjadi, dan **to** tidak dipakai untuk waktu di sini. Inggris Britania dan Amerika sama-sama benar; pilih salah satu dan pakai terus.

steps.title: Di mana letaknya?
steps.text: Sekarang kita bicara tentang tempat. Di mana HP-mu sekarang?
steps.body: Pakai **be** (is / are) + kata tempat: **in** (di dalam), **on** (di permukaan, menempel: *on the table*, *on the wall*), **under**, **next to**, **between** (dua hal: *between A and B*) dan **behind**. Kata-kata kecil ini disebut **preposisi** (kata depan). Bahasa Indonesia bilang *di bawah*, *di sebelah*, tapi dalam bahasa Inggris preposisinya sudah termasuk *di*: **under the table**, bukan 'in under the table'.

steps.title: Di sekitar rumah
steps.text: Ini kata-kata tempat di rumah sungguhan. Beberapa memakai there is / there are dari pelajaran sebelumnya.
steps.body: **between** selalu butuh dua hal: *between the window and the door*. Dan **on** tidak selalu *di atas*: jam **on** the wall menempel di dinding.

examples.en: The milk is in the fridge.
There is a clock on the wall.
There are two cats under the car.
examples.id: Ada dua kucing di bawah mobil.

examples.en: My desk is between the window and the door.
examples.id: Mejaku di antara jendela dan pintu.

examples.en: The garden is behind the house.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Kamu tidak bisa menemukan HP-mu. Ibumu tahu di mana letaknya.

options: Your phone is under the pillow.
Your phone is in under the pillow.
Your phone is on the pillow.
question.prompt: Kalimat mana yang artinya 'HP-mu di bawah bantal'?
question.explanation: **di bawah** = **under**. Bahasa Inggris tidak punya kata terpisah untuk *di*: **under** sudah berarti *di bawah*. Jadi pakai satu preposisi saja: **under the pillow**. 'in under' menambah kata yang tidak perlu, dan **on** artinya di atas.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Rina menunjukkan rumah barunya kepadamu.

question.solution: The bathroom is next to my bedroom.
question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Kamar mandinya di sebelah kamar tidurku.
question.explanation: **di sebelah** = **next to** (dua kata). Polanya benda + **is** + kata tempat: **The bathroom is next to my bedroom.**
